source.title: Sparse Double Descent in Vision Transformers: real or phantom threat?
source.authors: Victor Quétu; Marta Milovanović; Enzo Tartaglione

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures test performance across pruning-induced sparsity, testing a sparse form of double descent with a method different from the model-size and epoch sweeps in the claim's original sources.
record.gate_note: The paper's own pruning experiments and regularization ablation report outcomes relevant to sparse double descent. Background claims attributed to cited works are not recorded as results. The test-accuracy values in the figures are not numerically tabulated.
record.test_reason: The study's own pruning sweeps on ResNet-18 and ViT trace test accuracy against sparsity, a reduced-capacity axis rather than a width sweep. This bears on V1 by a different method. Its ℓ2 ablation on ViT bears on V6's claim that tuned regularization removes the peak. Neither original source is this paper.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly correct. The authors conclude that ViTs, like ResNets, show sparse double descent under pruning with label noise. Unlike CNNs, per cited prior work and not tested here on ResNet, ViTs can fully avoid it with optimally tuned ℓ2. The cost is reduced compressibility, and favoring SDD may suit compression goals.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies magnitude pruning and retraining across sparsity, rather than the original sources' model-size, epoch, or sample-size sweeps; it says the pruning setup follows He et al. [11].
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome changes with λ and label-noise rate: λ = 1 removes the pattern at ε ≤ 20% but only mitigates it at ε = 50%; λ = 3 makes performance monotonic in the reported settings. Dataset and architecture are also varied.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Image Analysis and Processing (ICIAP23)
record.problems: The plotted test-accuracy and test-loss values are not numerically tabulated; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The regularization ablation is conducted on ViT on CIFAR-10 with ε = 10%, while the broader regularization conclusions draw on the plotted CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 results.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 6 weight-distribution histograms are not included because they report parameter distributions rather than test performance or the double-descent pattern.

untested.parts: Conventional width or parameter-count growth is not tested, only pruning sparsity. Training accuracy is not reported, so the peak's location at the interpolation threshold is asserted but not shown.
Only deep networks are tested; no other model classes.
No effective-complexity measure and no comparison of peak locations across axes.

There is no zero-noise condition, so noise as the driver is not isolated. No multiple or triple peaks are examined. Regularization tuning is not tested on ResNet-18: the claim that CNNs cannot avoid SDD is cited from [20], not shown here.
There is no re-expression of the curve in terms of an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Increasing λ shifts the SDD bump toward smaller sparsity before it disappears. Higher λ also lowers the maximum achievable sparsity (compressibility cost), and λ>1 worsens performance.
missing.locator: Section 4, 'Study on λ' and 'Trade-off between SDD and compressibility'; Fig. 4

record.verdict_notes: All evidence is figure-only with no uncertainty estimates and no tabulated values. λ=1 was selected on a single setting (ViT, CIFAR-10, ε=10%) and then transferred. The λ=3 rows at ε≤20% appear to be extractor inventions. The pruning axis differs from the original model-size sweep, so V1 support is indirect (T2). The compressibility cost is not something V6 rules out, so it is not labeled limits_scope.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests pruning-induced sparsity, not a conventional sweep that adds model capacity from small to large.
No test-performance sweep over training epochs is reported.
The study does not vary the number of training samples.
The study tests sparse double descent in deep networks, not a general curve across model classes beyond deep networks.
The study does not compare peak locations across size, epoch, and sample axes or predict them with a single effective-complexity measure.
It varies synthetic label-noise rates and regularization, but does not test multiple or triple peaks, nor compare noisy labels with a zero-noise condition.
The study does not re-express the curve using an effective parameter count or test whether that makes it an ordinary U-shape.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 (λ=1e-4) and ViT (λ=0.03) under iterative magnitude pruning, CIFAR-10/100 at ε∈{10,20,50}% and CIFAR-100N
relationships.reason: The authors state SDD occurs for every ε, both models and CIFAR-100N (r1-r13, r7, r15). The values are figure-only and the capacity axis is pruning sparsity.
relationships.display_finding: Sparse double descent occurred along the pruning-sparsity axis for both architectures at 10%, 20%, and 50% injected noise and on CIFAR-100N.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: ResNet-18 (λ=1e-4) and ViT (λ=0.03) under iterative magnitude pruning, CIFAR-10/100 at ε∈{10,20,50}% and CIFAR-100N
source_check.reason: Section 4 explicitly reports sparse double descent for both architectures at every tested synthetic noise rate and on CIFAR-100N (r1-r13, r15). This is support along a pruning-based capacity axis.

relationships.condition: ViT with strong ℓ2 (λ=1 at ε≤20%, λ=3 at ε=50%)
relationships.reason: The curve becomes monotonic and the second descent vanishes (r17, r19, r23, r25, r22, r28). At λ=1 and ε=50% it is only mitigated (r21, r27). Fig. 4 shows flat test loss at λ=1 (r16).
relationships.display_finding: Curves became monotonic at λ=1 with ε≤20% and λ=3 with ε=50%, while λ=1 at ε=50% only weakened double descent and a λ=1 test-loss curve was flat.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: ViT with strong ℓ2 (λ=1 at ε≤20%, λ=3 at ε=50%)
source_check.reason: For this condition group the authors explicitly report disappearance of double descent and monotonic performance (r17, r19, r22, r23, r25, r28). The mitigated but persistent cases at λ=1, ε=50% (r21, r27) belong to a separate condition group and warrant limits_scope.

relationships.condition: ViT on CIFAR-10/100 with λ raised from 0.03 to 1 (ε≤20%) or 3 (ε=50%)
relationships.reason: Tuned ℓ2 flattens test loss (r16) and removes the peak (r17, r19, r22, r23, r25, r28). Higher noise needs stronger λ, since λ=1 leaves it at ε=50% (r21, r27), consistent with noise driving it.
relationships.display_finding: Increasing λ from 0.03 to 1 removed peaks at ε≤20%, while ε=50% required λ=3 because λ=1 retained a peak.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: ViT on CIFAR-10/100 with λ raised from 0.03 to 1 (ε≤20%) or 3 (ε=50%)
source_check.reason: The tested regularization component holds: λ=1 removes the peak at ε≤20%, while ε=50% requires λ=3 (r16, r17, r19, r21, r22, r23, r25, r27, r28). Multiple peaks and a causal noise/variance account are not established by these results.
